notes: The 4 groups reported by the connectivity check are genuinely four separate models in this booklet, so I deliberately left them unconnected: (1) the STOP sign on its round base (b1-b3, page 2), (2) the traffic light (b4-b11, page 3), (3) the white police hover sled (b12-b34, pages 4-8; the minifigure sits on it but is not a listed piece), and (4) the black bike (b35-b70, pages 9-19). Each has its own parts bubble, its own step numbering restarting at 1, and its own finished picture; the booklet never attaches one model to another. Joining them would invent connections the manual does not show. The two halves of the black bike (front b35-b53 and rear b54-b70) ARE joined, by axle b56 into b35 on page 18.
70 pieces: 11 for sign + traffic light, 23 for the hover sled, 19 for the front of the black bike, 17 for the rear engine section. Counts and colours match the parts list type by type.
Minifigure parts (heads, torsos, legs, helmet, backpack, etc.) and stickers are not in the parts list as lego-xxxx pieces, so they are not recorded.

Several attachment points are not clear from the small illustrations and are my best interpretation: which 1x4 brick carries the grilles/curved bricks/pin connectors on the hover sled, which bracket carries the slope/clip tile on the bike, and which clip holds which bar/handlebar.

Where a part clutches studs sideways (plates onto the 2x2 face of a bracket, curved bricks onto plates, grilles onto side studs) I recorded it in rests_on; clip, bar, pin, axle and peg joins are in other_joins.
The traffic-light antenna (b10) is pushed into the underside of the bottom brick and the base b11 is added last; modelled as other_joins with rests_on empty.
The blaster b28 is assumed to sit by its peg in pin-hole.2 of the second pin connector; the catalogue port clip.1 is used for it.
Orange round plates: b8 (traffic light) and b30 (blaster muzzle); Trans-Neon Green cone b49 is on the 6L bar.
